subject: Business
title: Marketplace Business Models
description: A quick win: understand Marketplace Business Models.

hook.text: eBay connects 135 million buyers and sellers. It doesn't own a single item in its catalog.

buildup.text: A marketplace connects supply and demand, taking a commission on each transaction without holding inventory.

discovery.text: The chicken-and-egg problem: buyers need sellers, sellers need buyers. Getting both sides started is the hardest part.

twist.text: Once a marketplace achieves liquidity — enough activity on both sides — it builds a self-reinforcing moat.

climax.text: Uber solved chicken-and-egg by subsidizing drivers first (guaranteeing fares), then riders came, then subsidies ended.

punchline.text: Own the marketplace, not the merchandise. Let others take the inventory risk.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge in starting a marketplace?
options: The chicken-and-egg problem: both buyers and sellers are needed simultaneously

details.summary: Marketplace businesses connect buyers and sellers on a platform, earning revenue through transaction fees without holding inventory. Amazon Marketplace, Uber, and Airbnb built massive businesses by facilitating exchanges rather than producing goods or services themselves.
details.whyItMatters: Marketplace models can scale to enormous size because they leverage participants' resources rather than their own capital. Understanding the chicken-and-egg problem and network effects is essential for building or investing in platforms.
takeaways: Marketplaces connect buyers and sellers and take a percentage of each transaction
Network effects make successful marketplaces increasingly hard to displace
The chicken-and-egg problem is getting both sides of the market to show up first

faq.question: What is the chicken-and-egg problem in marketplace businesses?
faq.answer: Buyers will not come without sellers, and sellers will not come without buyers. Solutions include subsidizing one side initially, starting in a single niche market, creating value for one side independent of the other, or seeding supply by recruiting directly.

faq.question: How do marketplace businesses prevent disintermediation?
faq.answer: Once buyers and sellers connect, they may transact directly to avoid fees. Platforms prevent this by providing insurance, payment processing, dispute resolution, reviews, and other value-added services that both parties lose if they leave the platform.
